claims.text: Mn in equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni produces magnetic frustration.
Mn-driven magnetic frustration lowers the effective stacking-fault energy of equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni.
Lower stacking-fault energy facilitates deformation twinning.
Lower stacking-fault energy facilitates stress-induced fcc-to-hcp transformation.
The combined activation of twinning and fcc-to-hcp transformation enhances work hardening.
The combined activation of twinning and fcc-to-hcp transformation alters failure modes.
Constituent count alone is inadequate to predict the alloys' mechanical properties.
The quinary Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy, equiatomic Cr-Fe-Co-Ni, and equiatomic Fe-Co-Ni can all be prepared as single-phase FCC materials after the stated thermomechanical processing.
Identical thermomechanical treatments can yield comparable grain sizes and defect densities across the three selected compositions.
In situ diffraction, TEM, and magnetic mapping can jointly resolve phase fractions, twins, dislocations, and deformation-associated magnetic-state changes.
Local stacking faults, twin density, and fcc-to-hcp transformation zones in the quinary alloy are influenced by Mn-driven magnetic interactions.
The quinary alloy undergoes a localized fcc-to-hcp transformation under strain.
Equiatomic Cr-Fe-Co-Ni has higher effective stacking-fault energy than equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni.
Equiatomic Fe-Co-Ni has higher effective stacking-fault energy than equiatomic Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni.
Relative to the quinary baseline, equiatomic Cr-Fe-Co-Ni will have lower twin density and delayed or suppressed fcc-to-hcp transformation.
Relative to the quinary baseline, equiatomic Fe-Co-Ni will deform predominantly by dislocation glide with minimal twinning.
The quinary baseline has measurable deformation twinning and a distinct onset of fcc-to-hcp transformation at room temperature.
Diffraction peak shifts can be used to infer local stacking-fault-energy variations in these alloys.
Failure to find greater twin density and earlier or greater fcc-to-hcp transformation in the quinary alloy than in the quaternary and ternary alloys would falsify the proposed mechanism.

contradictions.description: Equiatomic Cr-Fe-Co-Ni is described as a 'reduced-Mn' quaternary, but the stated composition contains no Mn. The mechanism then contrasts this quaternary with a ternary specifically characterized as lacking Mn, although both examples lack Mn.

The hypothesis assigns Mn a transformation-promoting role and assumes fcc-to-hcp transformation in the Mn-containing quinary baseline. The cited abstract instead reports that the fcc-to-hcp transformation occurs only in Mn-free CrCoNi and sets that ternary apart from the parent CrMnFeCoNi quinary.
